name: arpoison
why: A direct door into ARP cache poisoning, showing how a trusted local protocol can be quietly lied to.

brief.what_it_is: arpoison is a UNIX command-line utility described on its homepage as "The UNIX arp cache update utility." The homepage offers a source tarball (arpoison-0.7.tar.gz) and lists Libnet as a requirement. The page does not spell out its inputs or outputs. The name and the Brew description point to forging ARP entries on a local network, but the homepage itself does not state that.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no problem statement or author framing beyond the one-line description, so the reason for it is not stated there.
brief.install_notes: Source tarball from the homepage (arpoison-0.7.tar.gz). It requires Libnet, available at https://github.com/libnet/libnet, which must be installed first. The homepage gives no build steps, and I did not open the tarball. Homebrew lists the executable as arpoison.
brief.standout: A small, focused tool that does one thing: it updates ARP caches. The scout note frames it as a plain, direct demonstration of how a trusted local protocol can be fed false entries. I could not confirm the details from the homepage.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows version 0.7 and no date, release history, or commit activity. I did not fetch a repository or changelog.
brief.caveats: The homepage is very thin: one description line, a tarball link, a Libnet requirement, and an empty Contact section. I could not confirm usage, supported platforms, or licensing. The tarball is a binary download I did not read. Use on networks you do not own or control is a real concern for a tool with this name, so treat it as a security-research subject.
quotes: The UNIX arp cache update utility
fetch_log: http://www.arpoison.net/ — fetched OK; thin page with one description line, a source tarball link, a Libnet requirement, and an empty Contact section. No README, docs, or demo linked, so no further fetches.
